exposure: cefazolin (1 g) administered after the baby's umbilical cord was clamped
combined regimen of cefazolin (1 g intravenously) plus azithromycin (500 mg intravenously) given 30-60 minutes before the skin incision
Women with body mass index <30 kg/m2
Women with body mass index >30 kg/m2
Cefazolin plus azithromycin administered before skin incision
dual agent regimen but based the dose of cefazolin on the patient's body mass index: 2 g intravenously if the body mass index was <30 kg/m(2) and 3 g if the body mass index was >30 kg/m(2)
cohort: 6455 Women who underwent cesarean delivery at the University of Florida between January 2003 and December 2014
finding: The combination of cefazolin plus azithromycin administered before skin incision was significantly more effective in preventing postcesarean endometritis than cefazolin administered after cord clamping.
